summary: Weekly POC sync to review model selection signals, discuss version pinning strategy, and confirm rollback / fallback runbook. Customer saw regression on a small prompt subset with the newer quantized variant; team discussed pinning to a stable variant and staged fallback to a lower-cost model if latency spikes. Security and VPC constraints reviewed; next steps to share perf spreadsheet and run shadow test.
topics: Fallback models and automatic reroute policies
Next steps: benchmarks, security docs, dedicated capacity quote
transcript:
00:00 Maya: okay, welcome everyone, thanks for joining the weekly P O C sync for Atlas Financial. um today we want to focus on model selection and version pinning, and run through the rollback plan
00:12 Samir: yep thanks Maya, uh quick context, we ran the new quantized variant against 10k requests last night and saw a small but repeatable drop in answer completeness on our regulatory prompts
00:25 Ethan: yeah thanks for that, uh Lina could you share the exact example? I saw the email but want to make sure we reproduce it, sometimes transcription, sorry, sometimes tokenization differences cause changes
00:36 Lina: sure, um for prompt ID rf-998 it's basically the multi-step reconciliation question, and the quantized v1.3 returned truncated steps, it also hallucinated an extra account id, so we flagged it
00:49 Maya: okay, so two parts to discuss — do we pin to the prior float model 1.2 and use 1.3 for background traffic, or do we keep 1.3 but apply prompt-level overrides? what's the team's tolerance for cost vs latency
01:03 Samir: our SLO is p95 <= 600ms for user-facing flows, and cost is a secondary but important metric. if 1.2 gives better correctness but is higher cost, we might accept it for these regulatory flows only
01:18 Ethan: technically we can do per-route pinning in the config, so you can route reconciliation prompts to model-1.2-float and the rest to model-1.3-quant. fallback policy can also route to a cheaper model if latency or errors spike
01:32 Jared: curious about the KV cache impact — if we split routes will we lose the KV cache benefits and see latency increase?
01:39 Ethan: good question — prefix/KV cache is per model variant and per runtime. if you pin certain traffic to model-1.2, you'll warm separate caches. there's a tradeoff: initial cold-starts may be slightly slower but steady-state should be fine. we can pre-warm cache during the shadow run
01:55 Lina: is the observed hallucination definitely quantization artifact? could be prompt parsing differences too
02:02 Ethan: in our preliminary diffs it looks like token alignment and quantization rounding changed the logits in rare cases. not common, but enough for edge-case prompts. we have notes in the benchmark sheet, i'll upload the exact token diff
02:15 Maya: okay practical plan: pin critical routes to model-1.2 (float), set 1.3 as primary for others, and implement an automatic fallback to model-1.0-small if p95 > 1s or error rate rises above threshold
02:30 Samir: that seems reasonable — how do we test rollback? we want an ops-friendly runbook
02:36 Ethan: we have a one-click rollback API plus a staged canary. the sequence: push new pin config to 5% -> monitor metrics for 30m -> 25% -> 60m -> 100%. rollback is a single API call that flips the pin. we'll demo on staging and record it
02:51 Maya: we should document the runbook in the dashboard and include the exact API curl so your on-call can run it without our console
02:58 Jared: on networking — we need to confirm egress IPs and SAML SSO flow, and we also need guidance on KMS for encryption at rest for embeddings
03:08 Maya: yes, i'll send the security pack with SOC2 scope, KMS patterns and SSO notes. Ethan will include steps for audit log retention and per-route access control
03:20 Lina: are there recommended quantization profiles that are safer? maybe 8-bit vs 4-bit?
03:26 Ethan: we recommend 8-bit dynamic as default for sensitive flows; 4-bit is more aggressive and can introduce edge-case regressions. for Atlas we think 8-bit on non-regulatory flows, and keep float for regulatory ones
03:40 Samir: ok what about cost — can we get an estimate if 30% of traffic stays on float vs all quantized?
03:46 Maya: yes we'll add cost delta to the perf spreadsheet. Ethan, can you add a column showing tokens-per-request and cost-per-thousand for each pinned config?
03:55 Ethan: will do, i'll also add expected p95 and median and observed failure modes
04:02 Maya: one more thing — competitors were mentioned in procurement. Samir, you asked about how we compare to OpenAI + Anthropic on SLAs and private deployments
04:12 Samir: right, procurement wants to see our private deployment options and dedicated GPU pool SLAs, and they want a vendor comparison table
04:19 Maya: i'll include a short vendor mapping and our dedicated offering notes. we'll also share a draft PO template for the dedicated capacity quote call
04:28 Lina: for the shadow test, what's the recommended duration? we planned 24h but perhaps 48h is safer
04:34 Ethan: 48h with 10-20% sampled traffic is ideal for catching intermittent regressions. pre-warm caches and run the token-diff comparator overnight
04:44 Maya: great. quick recap — Redwood to share perf spreadsheet + pinned recommendations, SE to demo rollback on staging and record, customer to run 48h shadow test and share results, security docs + KMS notes from AE. we'll reconvene next week same time
04:58 Samir: thanks all
05:00 Maya: thanks everyone, bye
